back: $f$ takes a vector of $n$ real numbers and returns a vector of $m$ real numbers. Check these sizes before anything else.

front: Define $(g\circ f)(x)$. When is it defined?
back: $(g\circ f)(x)=g(f(x))$: apply $f$ first. Defined when the output space of $f$ matches the input space of $g$.

front: Why do ML systems use log-likelihoods?
back: A product of many probabilities underflows to 0 in floating point; $\ln\prod p_i=\sum\ln p_i$ is a well-scaled sum.
$m+\ln\sum_i e^{x_i-m}$ with $m=\max_i x_i$. All exponents become $\le 0$ so nothing overflows.
